**Short answer:**  
Yes. An individual salaried taxpayer can claim the **House‑Rent Allowance (HRA) exemption** under **Section 10(13A)** *and* also claim a **deduction for interest on a home‑loan** under **Section 80EEA** (or the applicable home‑loan interest provision), provided the separate conditions for each benefit are satisfied.  

---

### 1.  HRA exemption – Section 10(13A)

| Requirement | Provision |
|-------------|-----------|
| **Maximum exemption** – the exemption cannot exceed the lower of (a) 50 % of Basic + DA (or the HRA amount) or (b) the actual HRA received. | [C1] |
| **Percentage limit** – for non‑metro cities the exemption is capped at **40 %** of Basic + DA; for metro cities the cap is **50 %** of Basic + DA. | [C2] |
| **Regime condition** – the HRA exemption is **available only when the taxpayer opts for the old tax regime**. | [C1] |
| **Computation in the return** – the exemption is entered in Schedule 10(13A) and must be the lowest of the amounts prescribed (actual HRA, rent paid – 10 % of salary + DA, 40 %/50 % of salary + DA). | [C4] |

### 2.  Home‑loan interest deduction – Section 80EEA (first‑time home‑buyer)

| Requirement | Provision |
|-------------|-----------|
| **Deduction amount** – up to **₹ 50,000** of interest paid on a home loan is deductible, subject to the conditions in sub‑section (3) of Section 80EE. | [C6] |
| The deduction is a **separate head of income (“Income from House Property”)** and is claimed in Schedule VI‑A of the I‑TR. | (implicit from the statutory provision). |

### 3.  Interaction between the two benefits

* The law **does not prohibit** a taxpayer from claiming both benefits simultaneously.  
* The **HRA exemption** reduces the taxable salary component under the “Salaries” head.  
* The **home‑loan interest deduction** reduces taxable income under the “Income from House Property” head.  
* Because they operate on **different heads of income**, the same expenditure (rent vs. home‑loan interest) is not being double‑counted.
